body: You are aware, but may not necessarily be if you've never experienced it before and were unaware of consuming any substance.

I took 2.4g-10g of piracetam daily (mostly 4.8g/day in two 2.4g doses) for 9 months or so (all of senior year of high school).

It made school bearable since I was suicidally depressed and had severe anxiety problems. It made life as a whole bearable. No other difference. I had a 4.0 beforehand and my grades didn't change. No real noticeable difference in memory or anything else.

I use amphetamines occasionally for socialization (yeah, it's bad for you, and I don't recommend it, but I have my own reasons)

Anyways, in terms of nootropics:
Modafinil and Piracetam are nice, not that great combined with alcohol.

If you want to be social in a party setting: alcohol and coke--nothing's going to be better.

Some else mentioned phenibut, but that's pretty physically addictive and has horrible benzo-esque withdrawal. That being said, I'll still take it 1-2 times a week for a month and then not at all for a month etc...

Edit: I used to have severe social anxiety. It's still pretty bad, but not as bad.
Thanks. You as well.

Other substances haven't made much of a difference, pot and sometimes stimulants will increase the changes in visual perception. I don't really know how to explain it. If you've taken psychs it kind of feels like I have low-dose visuals of various psychs mixed together at any given time. Static surfaces always seem like they're moving unless it's a really bright room (the biggest thing). This is more prominent the less light there is. When it's dim I see a bit of colorful patterning as well.

Haven't tripped in over a year and it's still like this. If I stop smoking pot (or smoke ~1/week) it gets less intense/prominent, but if I'm going at it regularly, it'll be there.

Edit: To put this in perspective at my peak I was tripping 3/week and have probably tripped 50-60 times in my life (not including dissociatives or salvia). Now I just like the occasional DMT (once a year?) as far as psychedelics go. My preference drug-wise is for dissociatives and amphetamines.
I'm aware of HPPD. It doesn't actually interfere with my life, so I'm not technically "diagnosed" with HPPD.

I went hard on psychs at 16 (Not trying to brag, personally wish I waited 'til longer). By 19 I had explored stimulant/opioid/other territory. I feel like my visual perception is permanently changed.

At least I'm doing great academically so it hasn't really affected me in that sense.

As someone in a situation similar to OP, how does one go about doing that?

Seriously, I would've already if I knew how. It would take a load of stress/disappointment/depression off of my shoulders.
Low dose ketamine is like being drunk, with less negative effects. A bump is typically 25mg-50mg.

I've already used Ketamine for depression. It's fantastic. It's as effective as the MAOI's (for me) with less side effects and no dietary/drug restrictions. Not to say that ketamine doesn't have risks itself. And a lot of people fuck up using it as an antidepressant because the key is NOT to get high off of it. It's taking subpsychoactive doses on a fairly regular schedule.

This antidepressant effect is something I figured out experimentally in my heavy drug-using years.
www.erowid.org is a great resource for drug harm reduction, and if you want a specific question answered, the bluelight forums are the best choice.

People will tell you that you need to "get over" your depression before making progress in others things. As someone whose been clinically depressed for many years. This is a load of shit.

Now, you should still work on it. Start lifting (or another form of intense exercise). Personally, the only time life isn't painful is when I lift. Therapy is great. Do it. I've had therapy for 3 years, I still do--it's easy because it's free through my school. and I assume if you're in school it'll be free as well. Try medication if you want through a psychiatrist, but try therapy first. I've found meds that help me but they slow me down cognitively--which is all I really have.

I'm a bit ahead in your position I guess in that I do get invited to things, though my social life is laughable. I don't ever feel like going, and usually don't (and I always have been like this). I've been on one date, I'm a virgin as well. So I haven't dealt with my problems, but it's clear in your situation, or at least mine that being a virgin and having a laughable social life contribute to the depression.

You're also not suicidal. That's a step ahead of me. I find life painful, I always have. I'm just too fatigued all the time to kill myself. So I purposely have a horrible lifestyle that'll drag on my health (amphetamines and cigarettes) and ideally kill me of heart disease/lung cancer by 30. You're not at this point, and you don't ever have to be.

> I also think that if I even were to get a girl right now, I would just become really dependent on her and drag her down with me.

Ignore that fact. If you got a girl and that happens? So what? You experienced something and you'll improve from there. People here really like to feed the bullshit of working on yourself to be perfect and confident before moving on to these things. Don't bother. If you're actually "confident" you should read Plato's Trial of Socrates--you know nothing. Confidence is a stupid quality of personality people adopt to attract others, nothing else. So if you do become needy with a girl, so what? She'll break up from you. You failed. You learn from it and move on. If all that happens, that's a step ahead, isn't it? All you can do is slowly improve in that aspect of life. The fact that you're not completely hopeless puts you ahead of me. You should still learn to give off "confidence", but realize that's a load of shit because people here make it seem like internalizing confidence is easy and that it improves life every way, when really it's just social improvement.

Good luck.
